output.summary: A perennial herb native to Eurasia, including the British Isles, it spreads aggressively through rhizomes and has arrow-shaped leaves and reddish stems. Male and female flowers grow on separate plants and differ in colour. The sour leaves can be eaten raw or cooked, with the cooking water changed to reduce their strong taste.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves are eaten raw or cooked; changing the cooking water reduces their strong taste.
